However, the CFE (national one-stop business registration shop) reports having formalised over 7,000 companies nationally to date, and World Bank/IMF analyses describe Guinea-Bissau's economy as dominated by a highly informal, cashew-trading sector with a very small formal enterprise base. The score of 1 (<20%) is retained as the best available approximation; flagging for human review given the absence of a precise authoritative percentage.
revised_comments: Guinea-Bissau's formal business sector remains small relative to its predominantly informal, cashew-based economy. The Centro de Formalização de Empresas (CFE), the national one-stop shop for company registration, reports having formalised over 7,000 companies nationally to date. World Bank and IMF analyses describe a highly informal trading and agricultural sector, particularly around cashew exports, with a correspondingly narrow formal taxpayer and business base. Formal business registration coverage is estimated at below 20% of the total business population.
